correction.text: "The Old Copper complex of the Western Great Lakes"; "Major quarries were located on Isle Royale, the Keweenaw Peninsula, and the Brule River"; a burial ground and copper artifacts in Wisconsin; "who occupied the northern Midwest"

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page has no infobox; "Artifacts from some of these sites have been dated from 6500 to 1580 BCE" and "The Old Copper complex of the Western Great Lakes ... can be dated to around 6,500 BCE"; the burial ground was used "between around 4,000 and 2,000 BCE" and the Archaic-period page gives "4000-1000 BC: Old Copper complex emerges in the Great Lakes region". Wisconsin and a 150 km disc round Hancock (the Keweenaw Peninsula and Isle Royale) are drawn, 868 land cells; the page names no area or frontier.

ledger.note: 6000 BCE (project floor): the Old Copper complex is already working native copper round Lake Superior. "The Old Copper complex of the Western Great Lakes is the best known, and can be dated to around 6,500 BCE." The Archaic-period page and the burial-ground sentence ("between around 4,000 and 2,000 BCE") give later starts; the oldest date is used and the disagreement is in the notes.

ledger.note: 1580 BCE: the dated Old Copper artifacts end. "Artifacts from some of these sites have been dated from 6500 to 1580 BCE"; "By about 1,000 BCE, copper was increasingly restricted to jewelry and other status-related items, rather than tools". The next culture on the land is not named on the page.

certainty.note: Known from quarries and burials, not frontiers.

notes: Old Copper Complex, Western Great Lakes. The page is thin and has no infobox; the dates disagree: artifacts 6500-1580 BCE, burial ground and northern Midwest occupation 4000-2000 BC, Archaic-period page 4000-1000 BC. The dossier uses 6500 (clipped to the floor) to 1580 BCE, the page's own range for the complex; a gap-filler may prefer 4000-1000. Extent is Wisconsin plus the Keweenaw/Isle Royale disc (Michigan's Upper Peninsula, Minnesota and Ontario are not named on the page as culture area). The Great Lakes before and after (Laurentian Archaic, Woodland) have no dossier.
